profile_method.aggregation: Each internal value is the mean sum of that stage across all 12 layers per pass. Report the median/min/max of the three outer-job medians; preserve all nine internal values separately.
profile_method.caveat: CUDA-event intervals exclude metadata H2D and readback, include submission gaps, and may be perturbed by event insertion. These are not HTTP TTFT values.
profile_method.wall_method: Uninstrumented packed wall and synchronized temporary packed replay values are separate columns from instrumented stage intervals.
profile_method.packed_gpu_ms_header_meaning: Despite its historical column name, packed_gpu_ms is Instant host-wall time for repeated temporary graph launches plus a final synchronization, not CUDA-event GPU time. The graph includes complete packed prefill and greedy final selection; metadata H2D, D2H, and graph capture are excluded.

rejected_online_paged_prefill_ce.scope: Same printed CE as baseline for this limited sample; no additional precision inferred. Does not override deterministic generation rejection or establish final-candidate CE.

initial_online_generation.decision: Online q2-k32 rejected for default selection because deterministic complete-sequence equality failed. No tolerance weakened.

online_request_114_diagnosis.method: Teacher forcing: each decode consumes the preceding canonical monolithic token; same request RNG seed in each pass.
online_request_114_diagnosis.interpretation: Attention-dependent numerical drift reverses two nearly tied candidate ranks. The same draw still lands in rank 429, selecting a different token. Packed Reference is bit-exact and RNG advancement is identical in this reproduction.

final_profiles.scope: Alternating baseline/candidate outer jobs. Per-stage statistics use outer-job medians; wall and temporary graph totals are separately measured.
final_profiles.acceptance: Descriptive stage attribution only. These sparse and varying process envelopes do not establish a matched-clock kernel-only A/B; real-service acceptance uses its separate paired service runs.
final_profiles.envelope_assessment: Only 2-5 loaded samples per job; enforced limits span 115-133.24 W. Candidate-minus-baseline median SM clocks differ by -7.02% to +7.47%. Unchanged long-shape GEMM stages also improve by about 10-12%, so attention/wall deltas cannot all be attributed to the new attention kernel.
final_profiles.temporary_graph_scope: The same-process wall-versus-replay comparison includes launch, submission, synchronization and timing differences. It is not a direct launch-cost estimate or production cache-hit/service benefit measurement.

extended_paired_profiles.scope: Alternating baseline/candidate outer jobs. Per-stage statistics use outer-job medians; wall and temporary graph totals are separately measured.
extended_paired_profiles.acceptance: Descriptive observations only; excluded from causal stage-speedup acceptance because loaded clock envelopes differ. Candidate-only stage proportions identify remaining work.
extended_paired_profiles.envelope_assessment: Longer runs provide 9-18 loaded samples per job, with candidate-minus-baseline median SM clocks of -7.52/-4.33/-2.03% for short rows and +3.65/+5.28/+6.85% for long rows. Median enforced power differs by at most 1.94%, but clocks are not identical. Unchanged long GEMM stages also improve by about 3-5%; use these measurements for qualified stage attribution, not an exact fixed-clock attention-only speedup.
extended_paired_profiles.temporary_graph_scope: The same-process wall-versus-replay comparison includes launch, submission, synchronization and timing differences. It is not a direct launch-cost estimate or production cache-hit/service benefit measurement.

final_service.aggregation: Median/min/max of per-round statistics; p95 is a median of round p95 values, not a pooled percentile. Every round summary and actual runtime metric delta is retained.
final_service.comparison: Percent change is 100*(candidate/baseline - 1), paired by outer round. Lower is better for latency and gaps; higher is better for throughput. Envelope matching requires interpretation of recorded per-process samples.

configuration.baseline: Frozen starting commit with its Reference attention default.
configuration.candidate: CRUCIBLE_PREFILL_ATTN=exact-q4-k64 forced for the recorded comparison; subsequently selected as the same all-supported-geometry default, with no history threshold.
configuration.scope: A/B was recorded before the default spelling changed; parent audit confirms candidate dispatch and all other arguments are identical to the selected default.

envelope_comparison.scope: Loaded samples cover the complete outer benchmark, not specific scenarios or exact timed regions. Do not normalize timings by these samples or infer achieved occupancy.
envelope_comparison.assessment: Median clocks differ by under 1% in all three pairs; the first candidate has a 0.87% higher median enforced power limit. These are closely matched process envelopes, not identical per-kernel conditions. Small short-workload differences are within the scale of the observed variation.

final_scheduler_sweep.scope: Token budgets 256/512/1024 with chunking off; chunk caps 256/128/64 at budget 1024. No results implied for other combinations.
final_scheduler_sweep.envelope_assessment: Resumed round 3 has process-median loaded SM clocks about 1860-1867 MHz versus about 2760-2775 MHz in rounds 1-2. Within each round all six configuration medians are close; enforced power limits still differ. Retain every round, compare policies with the same-round budget-1024/no-cap control, and do not treat pooled absolute medians as one stable-clock experiment.
